source.title: Detecting Memorization in ReLU Networks
source.authors: Edo Collins; S. Bigdeli; S. Süsstrunk

record.file_problem: Text appears to contain the full paper, including appendix; some figure text and a reported correlation appear imperfectly rendered.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether activation-compression measures track memorization and generalization, using a different measure from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports correlations between compression-curve AuC and generalization error, plus early-stopping plots. It does not report the natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy comparison in V1 or test the specific conditions in V2–V8.
record.test_reason: The study uses random-label memorization to evaluate an activation-compression detector. Its results measure compression robustness and correlations with test performance, rather than any version's specified comparison. Perfect random-label training accuracy is reported, but the matched natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison required by V1 is not.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that NMF applied to deep single-class activations detects memorization and generalization across architectures and datasets, and can indicate early-stopping points, while acknowledging that definite guarantees require further analysis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses NMF compression of activations to assess layer non-linearity and its relationship to memorization or generalization; the claim versions concern other interventions, comparisons or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Compression method (NMF, PCA or random ablations) changes the reported correlation with generalization error; the authors describe NMF as most correlated.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 96 CIFAR-10 CNNs, activation-compression AuC correlates with test error: NMF -0.82, PCA -.064 as printed, and random ablations -0.61.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness to activation compression can indicate test performance across trained CNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: Across three CIFAR-10 training runs, smoothed test-loss minima nearly coincide with NMF-AuC maxima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NMF activation-compression AuC can indicate a useful early-stopping point.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretrained VGG-19 has a per-class correlation of 0.78 between NMF AuC and ImageNet test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NMF activation-compression AuC tracks per-class test accuracy.

record.problems: The paper reports correlations and plots, not uncertainty estimates for the correlations. The early-stopping evidence is described for three initializations and does not provide a numeric alignment measure. The supplied text renders the PCA correlation as -.064.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The paper's random-label experiments report training accuracy and compression behavior, but not the held-out accuracy result required for V1.

untested.parts: Matched training recipes showing natural-label held-out accuracy above chance and random-label held-out accuracy at chance. Perfect training accuracy across label-randomization levels alone does not establish this comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets; optimizer identities in the correlation grid are not reported as comparative results.
Large versus small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The states above concern applicability to the listed versions, not whether the compression findings occurred. Activation robustness is a different construct from V7's weight sharpness. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report held-out accuracy for natural versus randomized labels.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on image test error as described.
Optimizer conditions are included in a hyperparameter grid, but the study does not report adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance comparisons.
Measures activation compression robustness, not magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness.
Does not remove memorized training examples and measure the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: 96 CNN classifiers
rows.operation_detail: Compared compression-curve AuC with average test generalization error across a hyperparameter grid.

conditions.value: batch size, weight decay and optimization algorithm (SGD vs. ADAM)

rows.measure: Pearson correlation between AuC and average generalization error
rows.note: The text calls this the strongest correlation among the three methods.
rows.check: The reported correlation of -0.82 concerns activation compression, not V7's magnitude-aware weight perturbations or another version's effect.
